channel.title: Reachable — Guides
channel.description: Plain-language guides to the benefits and services seniors and people with disabilities in Victoria, BC can claim.

item.title: Start here: how the benefits system fits together
item.description: The benefits system is a set of doors, and some doors only open once you have opened another one first. This page shows you the order to do things in so you are not sent in circles.

item.title: Shared e-scooters and e-bikes: discounts, and what they mean if you have a disability
item.description: People ask us about Lime scooters. Victoria does not have a shared e-scooter — Lime rents e-bikes here. If you have a disability, a low income or a BC Bus Pass, Lime Access cuts the price by 80 per cent, but for most readers a $45 bus pass still beats it. This page also explains how to report a bike blocking a sidewalk or curb cut.

item.title: The RDSP: up to $1,000 a year, even if you never save a dollar
item.description: If you have the Disability Tax Credit and a low income, the government puts up to $1,000 a year into a savings plan for you — with no deposit of your own. You can also claim up to 10 past years.

item.title: Getting the PWD designation in BC
item.description: PWD is BC's disability designation. It pays a single person $983.50 a month plus up to $500 for rent, adds a free bus pass and dental and glasses coverage, and lets you earn $16,200 a year from work. If you are refused, free advocates in Victoria will take the appeal with you.

item.title: Help with rent, and help changing your home so you can stay in it
item.description: If you are 60 or older and rent, BC Housing can send you money toward the rent every month — and most people who qualify never apply. If a disability makes your home hard to live in, BC Housing can pay up to $20,000 for ramps, grab bars and a walk-in shower.

item.title: Getting around Victoria when travel is hard
item.description: If you are on disability assistance your bus pass is free, and a low-income senior pays $45 for a whole year. There is also a door-to-door bus, half-price ferries, an accessible parking permit, and up to $500 a year back on fuel tax.

item.title: Free help filing your taxes — and why filing unlocks the money
item.description: Filing a tax return is the switch that turns on almost every income-tested benefit, from the Guaranteed Income Supplement to the Canada Disability Benefit. Trained volunteers in Victoria file it for free, including past years you never filed.

item.title: The Disability Tax Credit: the one form that opens the rest
item.description: The Disability Tax Credit lowers the income tax you owe, and it is the door to the Canada Disability Benefit, the RDSP and other programs. There is no income test, and you can claim back up to 10 years.

item.title: Help paying for dentists, prescriptions and glasses
item.description: The Canadian Dental Care Plan covers dental work for people with no private insurance and a family income under $90,000. Fair PharmaCare cuts what you pay for prescriptions — but only if you register, and most people never do.

item.title: How to get cheap home internet, and a cheaper phone
item.description: If you get BC disability assistance, the Guaranteed Income Supplement, or the maximum Canada Child Benefit, home internet can cost $10 to $20 a month instead of the regular price. Here is who runs each program in Victoria, and exactly what to say when the first agent has never heard of it.

item.title: The Canada Disability Benefit: up to $204.20 a month
item.description: A monthly federal payment of up to $204.20 for people aged 18 to 64 who have the Disability Tax Credit and a low or modest income. Applying can also bring back pay for up to 24 months.
